transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Time: 11:00 AM PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Dev Patel (Redwood SE), Iris Nguyen (Redwood), Samir Patel (Hyperscribe CTO), Lena Ortiz (NLP Eng), Rajiv Menon (Privacy), Ava Cole (PM)

Summary (auto):
POC scoping to validate open-model shortlist for Hyperscribe's clinical note-generation workflow. Discussed success criteria (accuracy, hallucination rate, latency), workload sizing (concurrent sessions, token distribution), benchmarks and timelines. Agreed next steps include pricing, security docs, and a 1-week benchmark run using Redwood Dedicated or hosted with reserved capacity.

Topics: success criteria; model shortlist (Llama3 variants, Mistral-family, Falcon-180B-instruct-ish open variants); multilingual/medical domain needs; data residency and KMS; benchmarks and timelines

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. quick intros, we'll scope a POC around open models for the clinical note generation.
[00:15] Samir (CTO): Hi all, Samir here. we want to validate cost and quality tradeoffs before committing to a dedicated deployment. main use case: summarizing clinician notes + structured output for coding.
[00:28] Maya: Perfect. Dev is our SE who will run through latency/throughput questions. Dev?
[00:32] Dev (SE): Hey, yeah. quick note: we'll propose a short list of open models, run a couple benchmarks - ROUGE/med-specific metrics, hallucination checks. also need to size workload: concurrent writers, average tokens per request etc.
[00:46] Ava (PM): Our baseline: 500 daily active clinicians, peak 60 concurrent sessions, typical prompt ~250 tokens and expected output ~400 tokens. latency target is <1.2s per token for interactive flows, but for batch note generation 2-3s token is acceptable.
[01:05] Lena (NLP Eng): We care a lot about domain accuracy for medical abbreviations; hallucination is a showstopper. also multilingual: about 15% of notes in Spanish, occasional Portuguese. model must handle those or we need a fallback.
[01:22] Dev: ok noted. quick question on PII - will you be sending raw notes or de-identified text for the POC?
[01:28] Rajiv (Privacy): We'll send de-identified slices for the bench, but the long-term will be raw inside a VPC/private deployment. need KMS and audit logs.
[01:36] Maya: Perfect, that informs whether we propose Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. most customers start with hosted for speed, then move to Dedicated or Private when data residency/SOC2 matters.
[01:45] Samir: Timeline wise we want results in two weeks, deliverables: quality numbers, cost per note, latency profiles. is that realistic?
[01:52] Dev: Two weeks is tight but doable if the dataset slices and eval prompts arrive within 48 hours. main blockers are provisioning GPUs for the larger models and dataset curation.
[02:03] Iris (Solutions Eng): We'll try to use Redwood Dedicated reserved slots for the benchmark so the results reflect production latency. if you want purely hosted numbers we can do that too but may have more variance.
[02:15] Ava: For decision criteria, top priority: "no clinically actionable hallucination" threshold - we need hallucination rate <1% on critical fields; secondary is cost per note < $0.04, and latency target as mentioned.
[02:30] Maya: Great, we'll incorporate those as pass/fail and continuous metrics. now let's talk models - what's on your shortlist?
[02:36] Dev: For open models we suggest: Llama-3-13B-instruct quantized, Mistral-Instruct-22B variant, Falcon-180B-instruct (open checkpoint variants), and a smaller distilled Llama or Mistral-7B for latency-sensitive paths. also consider specialized medical fine-tuned checkpoints if you have in-house labels.
[02:57] Lena: Any of those handle Spanish well? we saw Llama-ish models sometimes degrade.
[03:02] Dev: Good point. Generally Mistral family has decent multilinguals; Llama-3 tends to be strong with few-shot Spanish when prompted, but we should test. for clinical language, off-the-shelf models vary - we anticipate quality tradeoffs and may need light fine-tuning or retrieval augmentation.
[03:18] Samir: About hallucination testing - what metric do you run?
[03:21] Dev: We run precision on extracted entities, factuality checks against the note, and a scored hallucination rubric. we'll include both automated checks and a small human evaluation sample for edge cases.
[03:33] Rajiv: Security: For POC we need encrypted at rest, KMS-managed keys, SSO support and audit trail. can you share SOC2 docs?
[03:41] Maya: Yes we'll share SOC2 and architecture notes. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering; Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools with audit logs.
[03:51] Lena: On scaling - if we see good perf, what's the path to production? e.g., dedicated capacity?
[03:57] Dev: Usually POC -> Dedicated reserved pool for predictable latency -> Private if you need on-prem or strict residency. we can show cost delta between hosted and dedicated; Dedicated typically reduces latency variance and unit cost at scale.
[04:12] Ava: Can you show us an example cost calc? I want cost per note for 100k notes/month.
[04:17] Maya: We'll include that in the proposal. rough back-of-envelope now: depends on model size and batching; smaller models cheaper but quality tradeoff. we'll run bench to give exact numbers.
[04:27] Dev: For the benchmark we'll capture token throughput, p50/p90 latency, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:35] Samir: About datasets: we'll provide three slices: short notes, long consults, and Spanish notes. how many samples do you need?
[04:42] Dev: For initial bench 200 samples per slice is good; plus 50 examples for human eval. makes bench quick but representative.
[04:51] Lena: We can deliver that by Friday.
[04:54] Rajiv: One more Q on chain-of-trust: do you support hardware HSM for keys or bring-your-own HSM?
[05:01] Maya: Private deployments can integrate with customer KMS/HSM; we'll include integration notes.
[05:07] Ava: On multilingual fallback - if Spanish quality is poor, can we route Spanish to a different model?
[05:12] Dev: Absolutely; Redwood supports smart routing by policy (language detection -> model). we can also set fallbacks for cost vs quality.
[05:20] Samir: Any concerns about open model licensing? we need to ensure a compliant usage path.
[05:24] Maya: We'll review licenses; most open checkpoints are permissive but we'll call them out in the docs.
[05:29] Dev: quick note: Falcon open checkpoints vary, and some big-family weights may have usage clauses. we will vet.
[05:35] Ava: Ok let's talk pass/fail thresholds one more time so it's explicit.
[05:39] Maya: Pass if: hallucination rate on critical fields <1%, entity extraction F1 >= 0.92, average latency per token <=1.5s in peak scenario, and cost per note <= $0.04. Anything outside requires remediation plan.
[05:55] Rajiv: If you need more stringent auditability we'll push Private. we'll review security docs first.
[06:01] Dev: For the POC protocol: 1) Hyperscribe sends slices and prompts, 2) Redwood provisions Dedicated benchmark slots, 3) Run benchmarks across shortlisted models and smaller fallbacks, 4) Deliver metrics and human eval, 5) Follow-up decision meeting.
[06:18] Maya: Good. on models: specifically we'll bench Llama-3-13B-instruct (q4_0), Mistral-Instruct-22B, Falcon-180B-open-instruct, and a Mistral-7B distilled. if you want a medical-finetuned checkpoint we'll include one experiment if you can provide 1k labeled samples.
[06:35] Lena: We'll see if we can share that. 1k might be hard but 300 labeled examples available.
[06:40] Dev: That's still useful for a small fine-tune/adapter test.
[06:44] Ava: Can you also include suggested prompt templates so we can replicate?
[06:48] Iris: yes we'll include prompt templates and the evaluation harness (script + metrics).
[06:52] Samir: anything else on timeline? we need results to present to execs by Aug 6. that's two weeks from now.
[06:59] Maya: We'll aim for that but need dataset slices by Jul 23. Dev will provision by Jul 24 and bench runs Jul 25-28.
[07:08] Dev: We'll try to do baseline hosted runs sooner while Dedicated slots are being scheduled to save time.
[07:14] Rajiv: Cost model - what's the expected committed spend for Dedicated?
[07:18] Maya: i'll include reserved slot tiers in the proposal; can do a short term monthly commit for the pilot.
[07:24] Samir: ok thanks team. quick recap?
[07:27] Maya: Recap: Hyperscribe will provide 3 data slices + sample prompts by 2026-07-23; Redwood sends POC proposal/pricing/SOC2 docs by 2026-07-23; Dev provisions bench infra by 2026-07-24; benchmark run week of Jul 25; deliver results & human eval by Jul 28; follow-up decision meeting scheduled for Aug 6.
[07:52] Ava: sounds good. thanks.
[07:55] Maya: Thanks everyone. we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the Aug 6 review and attach docs.
[07:59] END

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings of model names ("Lama" for Llama, "Mistral 22" as "Mistral 22B-variant"), and some speaker labels may be abbreviated.
